title: Megalopolis: Can Film Change Our World? Is It Supposed to?

commenti.body:
I haven't seen it yet (even more excited after the absolute pasting it has received critically because I love ridiculous, interesting, malfunctioning works with singular ambitions) and obviously many, many would disagree with everything in your post but this was well said and nice to read. 
Did you foresee Megalopolis ever having a critical reappraisal? Will time ever bend towards Coppola's vision here or is it too goofily earnest and impressed with itself? (These seem to be the most common complaints).

100% it will be reappraised. Even just on a technical level there are some awe-inspiring sequences. But I think the main problem is that people think it's impressed with itself, when really it's just a fun comedy. Coppola made The Godfather and Apocalypse Now and assume he's full of himself. He also made Peggy Sue Got Married and Jack.

I'm sorry it's a terrible film. An egotistical, self-indulgent horrendous mess, and the desperate attempts to intellectualise it are pathetic. If you want film as a tribute to itself, with all its playfulness, silliness, joy and hope, there are plenty of genuine masterpiece blockbusters out there that cater to such. Coppola's intention was not that and the unbearable pretention puts paid to any hints that it is in any way self-aware. The nearest insight from this film I can gain is that is is a reflection of Coppola's lack of self-awareness, whether it be his tawdry behaviour in making the film or defending a vile, convicted paedophile. This film is as worthy an epitaph to his filmmaking career in that it reflects the state of the man as he is at this moment in time.

I don't understand how it was incoherent. It's not a plot-driven film, there's nothing to follow (or fail to follow.) It's a series of scenes driven primarily by visuals.

You can say his "intention was not that," I can say it was, we can go back and forth forever because neither of us know. But the only way you can assume it's not aware of itself is if you already look down on Coppola and I don't.

Also, don't say sorry and then follow it up by calling me pathetic- just call me pathetic, it's more honest 😊
You aren't pathetic for liking it or writing this post. This post has me excited to see the film in theatres, so thanks for speaking up against the current.
I'm glad to hear that! Maybe you won't dig it and that's okay. At least try to give it a fair shot.
